hero.eyebrow: Al Haram · Giza · the eleventh floor
hero.title: Eleven floors up, the pyramids are the view from your bed
hero.lead: A guest house on the top floor of an ordinary Giza apartment block, which is the whole point: at this height you stand level with the base of the Great Pyramid, and the rooftops of Al Haram fall away below Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.

facts.view: Level with the Great Pyramid's base

sections.day: A day on the eleventh floor

rooms.intro: Twelve rooms on one floor. Two kinds face west, straight at the plateau; the studio has a sofa and the same window; the city twin looks east over Al Haram and costs the least. All have air conditioning, a private bathroom and a fridge.
rooms.stay: By the night, for a few days or a longer stay: ask us
rooms.bathroomText: Breakfast is served on the open roof terrace from seven to nine, with the plateau laid out in front of you; in the evening it is where guests sit for the sound-and-light show. Tea and coffee all day.

double-view.name: Double room, pyramids view
double-view.desc: A double bed and a single, a small table at the window and the three pyramids beyond the balcony railing. The room most guests write home about: wake up to Khufu, watch the sun go down between Khafre and Menkaure.

twin-view.name: Twin room, pyramids view
twin-view.short: Two beds, pyramids in the window
twin-view.desc: Two beds with velvet headboards and a window that frames the plateau. For friends, colleagues or a parent and child, with the same view as the double.

studio.name: Deluxe studio
studio.short: A queen bed and a sitting area
studio.desc: A queen bed with room to sit: a sofa, a table and the window onto the pyramids. The largest room on the floor, for a longer stay or a couple who wants space.

twin-city.name: Twin room, city view
twin-city.desc: Two single beds and a window over the rooftops of Al Haram. The simplest room, a few steps from the lounge and the roof where the view is.

view.title: What you see from the balcony
view.text: The guest house faces due west across the rooftops of Al Haram to the plateau. From left to right: Menkaure, the smallest; Khafre, which looks tallest because it stands on higher ground and still wears its casing at the top; and Khufu, the Great Pyramid. At sunset the sun drops between them.

giza.intro: The house is in Al Haram, the district that grew up along Pyramids Road, a long straight avenue from the Nile to the plateau. West is the site; north is the new museum; east, past the metro, is Cairo proper. South along the river are the older pyramids, Saqqara and Dahshur, where the builders practised.
giza.byAir: From Cairo Airport: about an hour by car across the city; the house arranges pickup. From Sphinx Airport: 40 minutes on the desert road.
giza.byMetro: Metro Line 2 to El Monib, then a short taxi ride down Al Haram road.
giza.byRoad: By car: Al Haram (Pyramids) Road from the Nile, turn south at Abd Al Aziz Al Basel Street.

elev.title: Profile from the house to the plateau
elev.roofs: rooftops of Al Haram, about {m} m
elev.note: Heights are approximate; the vertical scale is stretched 2.5 times.
elev.caption: The eleventh floor stands at roughly {floor} m above the sea, the base of the Great Pyramid at {base}: the whole pyramid rises above the rooftops in front of you.
elev.text: Al Haram is flat and low. The plateau to the west rises about forty metres above it, and the pyramids stand on top of that rise. From a ground-floor window you would see apartment blocks. From the eleventh floor the line of sight clears the roofs, and all three pyramids stand against the sky, base to apex.

day.title: A day on the eleventh floor
day.hint: Drag the sun round the ring, or tap a moment.

dawn.d: The sun comes up behind you, over Cairo, and lights the pyramids from the east. The clearest view of the day is in the first hour.

breakfast.d: Seven to nine on the open terrace: ful, falafel, eggs, bread, white cheese, fruit, tea. The plateau is laid out in front of your table.

checkout.d: Check-out is at eleven; the Sphinx entrance is a short ride down the road. Go early, before the coaches and the heat.

checkin.d: Rooms are ready from two. Midday haze flattens the view; it is a good hour for the air conditioning and a sleep.

afternoon.d: By four the light turns and the pyramids come back out of the haze. The balcony faces them squarely.

sunset.d: The sun drops behind the plateau. Depending on the month it sets to the left of Menkaure or between Khafre and Khufu; in late October it is on the left.

dusk.d: Twenty minutes of pink and violet, the pyramids as cut-outs, the lights of Al Haram coming on below.

show.d: The plateau is lit in colour from the Sphinx side. You watch it from the terrace, with the commentary carrying up on still nights.

night.d: The pyramids go dark; the city does not. The lift runs all night and someone is at the desk.

practical.intro: What the listings say, in one place.
items: Air conditioning, a private bathroom and a fridge in every room; Wi‑Fi throughout; a lift to the eleventh floor.
Check-in from 14:00, check-out by 11:00, breakfast 07:00 to 09:00. Someone is at the desk all night.
Airport pickup for a fee: give us your flight. Metro Line 2 to El Monib, then a taxi down Pyramids Road.
